newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak key money M2 rises 15.7 pct yr/yr in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Slovak key money M2 rises 15.7 pct yr/yr in 1996.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Monday its key money supply measure, M2, rose 15.7 percent in 1996 after a 20.7-percent rise in 1995.
Head of the NBS's Monetary Analyses Department, Milos Tkac, told Reuters that M2 totalled 413.4 billion crowns ($12.7 billion) as of December 31, 1996, after 357.0 billion as of December 31, 1995.
SLOVAK MONEY SUPPLY FY 1996 JAN-NOV 96 FY 1995 FY 1994
Note. The NBS's full-year target was an M2 expansion of 11.6 percent year-on-year. M2 measures currency, demand and time deposits, savings deposits and foreign currency deposits.
